summary: Nine labels declare chlorogenic acids (40 to 50% where a percent is printed; 176168 prints none), including CoffeeGenic and Svetol. Thirteen print a green coffee extract with no chlorogenic acid figure: 330008, 330971, 330972, 330973 print 10:1 at 800 mg; 312583 to 312586 and 312901 print Coffea arabica bean extract; 252516, 253660, 253665, 253672 print extract at 250 mg. Where a purpose shows, it is weight or metabolic (59208 and Decaf Thermo Igniter); 73326 prints antioxidant support. Meta-analyses of randomized trials find body weight -1.23 kg (32507437) and -2.47 kg with all studies at high risk of bias (20871849), while another of 16 trials finds no significant change in body weight (31398662). A 12-week trial of 800 mg/day of decaffeinated extract in 44 obese breast cancer survivors found no significant effect (36134465). The one trial with a verified dose (16820341) gave 140 mg/day chlorogenic acid to 28 people with mild hypertension, reports blood pressure within groups, and matches no label purpose. Abstracts only. Reference only, no Evidence credit.
question_for_clinician: Do pooled weight results of -1.23 kg (32507437) and -2.47 kg with all trials at high risk of bias (20871849), against a null pooled weight result (31398662) and a null 800 mg/day RCT (36134465), support any credit for labels printing a chlorogenic-acid standardized green coffee extract? 16820341 is the closest single trial with a stated dose but is a 28-person blood pressure study. A second point: the 13 labels with no chlorogenic acid figure have no matching studied amount. Agent recommendation: no credit for all 22.
